- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 0.5–1.5 units.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizons; if forecast is >1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 0.3–0.7 units.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.2–0.8 units in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by 0.1–0.4 units downward.
